text: EX-10.1 2 boum_ex10z1.htm AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO ASSET AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS PURCHASE AND TRANSFER AGREEMENT, DATED NOVEMBER 24, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN BOUMARANG INC. AND SHORE HOUSE IVF AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO ASSET AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS PURCHASE AND TRANSFER AGREEMENT This Amendment No. 1 (this “Amendment”) is made as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”) between BOUMARANG, INC., a Delaware corporation (“Buyer”), and SHORE HOUSE ÍVF, a Faroe Islands company, registration no. 6472 (“Seller”). Capitalized terms not defined here have the meanings given in the Purchase Agreement. RECITALS A. The Parties are parties to the Asset and Intellectual Property Rights Purchase and Transfer Agreement made as of December 31, 2024 (the “Purchase Agreement”), filed as Exhibit 10.4 to Buyer’s Registration Statement on Form S-1, File No. 333-292164 (the “Filed Version”), under which Seller transferred to Buyer the intellectual property and related assets listed on Exhibit A thereto, including U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 63/727,652, “Self-Righting and Self Stabilizing Unmanned Surface Vessel” (the “Assets”). B. The Closing occurred effective December 31, 2024 (Buyer) / January 1, 2025 (Seller) (the “Closing Date”). Buyer issued 3,500,000 shares of common stock valued at $3,500,000 to Seller (the “Consideration Shares”) and Seller delivered the Assets. C. The provision of the Purchase Agreement captioned “Clawback Provision,” beginning “Notwithstanding anything contrary in this Agreement, this transaction shall be reversed if Boumarang does not successfully uplist...” (shown as Section 1.2 in the Filed Version), however numbered in any executed or filed version (the “Clawback Provision”), provides for reversal of the transaction if Buyer does not uplist on a National Exchange within twelve (12) months after the Closing Date. Buyer did not uplist within that period. Neither Party demanded or effected a reversal: the Consideration Shares were not returned and the Assets were not reassigned. D. Neither Party wishes to reverse the transaction. The Parties have mutually agreed that the transfer of the Assets shall stand, and wish to terminate the Clawback Provision, confirm Buyer’s ownership of the Assets, and release one another from any claim arising out of the Clawback Provision. E. Concurrently with this Amendment, the Parties are executing a separate Exclusive Faroe Islands Distribution Agreement (the “Distribution Agreement”), which replaces the Reseller Authorization Agreement attached as Exhibit B to the Purchase Agreement. The two documents are executed as part of a single transaction, and each supports the other as consideration. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and releases below, the concurrent execution of the Distribution Agreement, and One Hundred Dollars ($100.00) paid by Buyer to Seller, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows: 1. Termination of the Clawback Provision 1.1 The Clawback Provision is deleted from the Purchase Agreement in its entirety, however it is or may be numbered in any executed or filed version. Each reference in this Amendment to a provision of the Purchase Agreement is controlled by the caption and quoted opening words used to identify it; any section number is a secondary, non-operative aid based on the Filed Version, and a difference between that number and the number in any executed version does not affect this Amendment. 1.2 Each Party, for itself and its affiliates, waives in full and agrees not to exercise or assert any right to reverse, unwind or rescind the transaction under the Clawback Provision or otherwise, whether that right is alleged to have arisen before or after the Effective Date. The Parties confirm that the transactions contemplated by the Purchase Agreement have at all times remained in effect: the Assets have remained with Buyer since the Closing Date and the Consideration Shares have remained with Seller. No listing on a National Exchange, and no statement in the recitals to the Purchase Agreement regarding a planned listing, is a condition to or obligation in respect of Buyer’s ownership of the Assets or Seller’s retention of the Consideration Shares. 2. Confirmation and Present Assignment of the Assets 2.1 Seller confirms that the Parties intended all right, title and interest in and to the Assets to pass absolutely to Buyer at the Closing, and that Buyer has held and exercised ownership of the Assets since the Closing Date. 2.2 To the extent any right or interest in the Assets remained in Seller, was imperfectly conveyed, or vested or revested in Seller by operation of the Clawback Provision, law or equity, Seller hereby presently, absolutely and irrevocably assigns, conveys and quitclaims that right and interest to Buyer, throughout the world, as of the Effective Date. Seller retains no ownership, license, reversionary, compensation or other proprietary interest in the Assets. 2.3 Concurrently with this Amendment, Seller is executing and delivering the Confirmatory Assignment attached as Annex I, in recordable form. 2.4 The Distribution Agreement is a personal contractual right to resell finished products. It is not a patent, copyright or trade-secret license and is not a lien, security interest or other encumbrance on the Assets. Its expiration, invalidity or termination does not affect Buyer’s ownership of the Assets or any release or assignment in this Amendment. 3. Mutual Release 3.1 Each Party, for itself and its affiliates, successors and assigns, releases the other Party and its officers, directors, shareholders, affiliates, successors and assigns from all claims, whether known or unknown, arising out of or relating to the Clawback Provision, Buyer’s failure to uplist on a National Exchange, or any alleged reversal or failure to effect a reversal of the transaction. Each Party waives California Civil Code Section 1542 as to those claims only. 3.2 This release is limited to the matters described in Section 3.1. It does not release any other claim, representation, warranty, covenant or obligation under the Purchase Agreement, including the provision captioned “Registration Rights,” beginning “Buyer and Seller shall negotiate and execute” (shown as Section 9 in the Filed Version), or any obligation created by this Amendment or the Distribution Agreement. 4. Consideration Shares 4.1 The Consideration Shares are fully earned, non-refundable and non-forfeitable as of the Closing Date. Seller has no obligation to return, surrender or cancel them, and Buyer has no right to claw them back. The Consideration Shares remain subject to applicable restrictions on transfer under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. 5. Seller Representations Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as of the Effective Date that: (a) Seller is validly existing under the laws of the Faroe Islands and has full power and authority to enter into this Amendment and Annex I, and their execution, delivery and performance have been duly authorized by all action required under applicable law and Seller’s constitutional documents; (b) Seller has not sold, assigned, licensed, pledged or encumbered any of the Assets, or any claim under the Clawback Provision, to any person other than Buyer; and (c) to Seller’s knowledge, each inventor, author and contributor whose work is included in the Assets has assigned that work to Seller or directly to Buyer in writing, and no such person retains any ownership or compensation right in the Assets. 6. Further Assurances and Recordation 6.1 Seller shall execute and deliver any further assignment, declaration, consent or other instrument Buyer reasonably requests to confirm, record or perfect Buyer’s title to the Assets with the United States Patent and Trademark Office or any other registry or authority, and shall use reasonable efforts to obtain comparable instruments from its personnel and contributors. Buyer shall bear the cost of recordation and of instruments requested after the Effective Date, except where the need arises from a breach by Seller. 6.2 If Seller does not execute a reasonably requested instrument within ten (10) business days after written request, Seller appoints Buyer and each officer of Buyer as its attorney-in-fact, coupled with an interest, solely to execute and file that instrument in Seller’s name to confirm or record a transfer already effected. 6.3 Notwithstanding the provision of the Purchase Agreement captioned “No Recordation,” beginning “Neither this Agreement nor a memorandum hereof” (shown as Section 12.10 in the Filed Version), Buyer may record this Amendment, Annex I or a registry-specific short-form assignment with any intellectual property registry or governmental authority, and may file or furnish this Amendment and the Distribution Agreement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission or any other regulator. Seller authorizes each such authority to record Buyer as owner. 7. Survival 7.1 Sections 1 through 3 and Section 5, and Annex I, survive without limitation as to time, notwithstanding the provision of the Purchase Agreement captioned “Survival,” beginning “The terms, covenants, agreements, representations and warranties” (shown as Section 12.6 in the Filed Version). This addresses contractual survival only and does not alter any applicable statute of limitations. All other survival provisions of the Purchase Agreement are unchanged. 8. General 8.1 Except as expressly amended here, the Purchase Agreement remains in full force and effect and is ratified. Ratification does not revive the Clawback Provision or create any condition on Buyer’s ownership of the Assets. In any conflict between this Amendment and the Purchase Agreement, this Amendment controls. 8.2 This Amendment is governed by California law. The provision of the Purchase Agreement captioned “Arbitration,” beginning “This Agreement shall not be subject to termination” (shown as Section 10.2 in the Filed Version), applies to this Amendment, except that either Party may seek provisional equitable relief in a court of competent jurisdiction. The references to “Section 8” in the provision of the Purchase Agreement captioned “Governing Law” are corrected to refer to that arbitration provision. 8.3 This Amendment may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which is an original. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Amendment as of the Effective Date. BOUMARANG, INC. By: /s/ Craig Nehrkorn Name: Craig Nehrkorn Title: Chief Executive Officer Date: November 18th 2026 SHORE HOUSE ÍVF By: /s/ DANIAL HOYDAL Name: DANIAL HOYDAL Title: CEO Date: NOVEMBER 24th 2026 ANNEX I — CONFIRMATORY ASSIGNMENT For good and valuable consideration received under the Asset and Intellectual Property Rights Purchase and Transfer Agreement made as of December 31, 2024, as amended (the “Purchase Agreement”), SHORE HOUSE ÍVF, a Faroe Islands company, registration no. 6472, J. Paturssonargøta 72, FO-100 Tórshavn, Faroe Islands (“Assignor”), confirms the transfer made at the closing under the Purchase Agreement and hereby presently sells, assigns, transfers, conveys and quitclaims to BOUMARANG, INC., a Delaware corporation, 200 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine, California 92618 (“Assignee”), its entire right, title and interest throughout the world in and to: (a) U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 63/727,652, “Self-Righting and Self Stabilizing Unmanned Surface Vessel”, filed December 3, 2024, and U.S. Non-Provisional Patent Application No (attorney docket BLMR-001P), together with all patents issuing from either and all continuations, continuations-in-part, divisionals, reissues, reexaminations, substitutes, extensions, PCT and national-phase applications claiming priority to or benefit of either, in any jurisdiction; (b) all inventions, know-how, trade secrets, specifications, drawings, CAD files, bills of materials, software, test data and documentation described or embodied in the foregoing; (c) all copyrights, trademarks, trade dress, logos and domain names relating to the WaveDrone, including the presentation film and footage, pitch deck, Eureka brochure and other marketing and branding collateral, together with the associated goodwill; and (d) all claims and causes of action for past, present and future infringement or misappropriation of any of the foregoing, and all remedies for them. Assignor represents that it has not assigned, licensed, pledged or encumbered the foregoing except for the transfer to Assignee, and that it retains no ownership, license or reversionary right in it. The Exclusive Faroe Islands Distribution Agreement between the parties is a contractual right to resell finished products and is not an encumbrance on the rights assigned here. Assignor requests and authorizes the Commissioner for Patents, the U.S. Copyright Office and the corresponding authority of each other jurisdiction to record this assignment or a registry-specific short-form assignment and to issue all patents and registrations in Assignee’s name. Assignor will execute any further instrument Assignee reasonably requests to record, perfect or defend title, at Assignee’s expense. This assignment confirms the transfer intended at the closing and, to the extent any interest remained in or later vested in Assignor, presently assigns that interest as of the date signed below. It is governed by California law, except that title, validity and recordation of a registered right are governed by applicable federal law and the law of the jurisdiction of registration. title: Jackson Acquisition Co II
text: EX-10.1 3 ea031343501ex10-1.htm AMENDED AND RESTATED INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT TRUST AGREEMENT, DATED AS OF NOVEMBER 24, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN THE COMPANY AND CONTINENTAL STOCK TRANSFER & TRUST COMPANY Exhibit 10.1 AMENDED AND RESTATED INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT TRUST AGREEMENT This Amended and Restated Investment Management Trust Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is made effective as of November 24, 2026, by and between Jackson Acquisition Company II, a Cayman Islands exempted company (the “ Company ”), and Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company, a New York corporation (the “ Trustee ”), and amends and restates in its entirety that certain Investment Management Trust Agreement, dated as of December 9, 2024, by and between the Company and the Trustee (the “ Existing Agreement ”). WHEREAS , the Company’s registration statement on Form S-1 (File No. 333-282393) (the “ Registration Statement ”), and prospectus (the “ Prospectus ”) for the initial public offering of the Company’s units (the “ Units ”), each of which consists of one of the Company’s Class A ordinary shares, par value $0.0001 per share (each, an “ Ordinary Share ”), and one right to receive one-tenth (1/10) of one Ordinary Share (such initial public offering hereinafter referred to as the “ Offering ”), was declared effective on December 9, 2024 by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; and WHEREAS , on December 11, 2024, the Company consummated the Offering; and WHEREAS , the Company has entered into an Underwriting Agreement (the “ Underwriting Agreement ”) with Roth Capital Partners, LLC (“ Roth ”), as representative of the several underwriters (the “ Underwriters ”) named therein; and WHEREAS , as described in the Prospectus, $232.3 million of the gross proceeds of the Offering and sale of the Private Placement Units (as defined in the Underwriting Agreement) was delivered to the Trustee to be deposited and held in a segregated trust account located at all times in the United States (the “ Trust Account ”) for the benefit of the Company and the holders of Ordinary Shares included in the Units issued in the Offering (the amount delivered to the Trustee and any Monthly Extension Payments (as defined below) (and any interest subsequently earned thereon) are collectively referred to herein as the “ Property ,” the shareholders for whose benefit the Trustee shall hold the Property will be referred to as the “ Public Shareholders ,” and the Public Shareholders and the Company will be referred to together as the “ Beneficiaries ”); and WHEREAS , the Company has entered into that certain Business Combination Marketing Agreement, dated as of December 9, 2024, with Roth, pursuant to which the Company will pay Roth a cash fee (the “ Marketing Fee ”) for certain advisory services upon the consummation of the Company’s initial Business Combination (as defined below) in an amount equal to up to $9.2 million; and WHEREAS , if a Business Combination (as defined below) is not consummated by December 11, 2026, upon the request of Sponsor, the Company may extend the period of time the Company has to consummate its initial Business Combination (as defined below) by up to twelve total additional months (or within 36 months from the consummation of the Offering) (each such month, a “ Monthly Extension Period ”), provided, that for each Monthly Extension Period, the Sponsor (or its affiliates or designees) deposits into the Trust Account an amount equal to the lesser of (i) $250,000 and (ii) $0.02 for each public share that is not redeemed immediately preceding such Monthly Extension Period (each, a “ Monthly Extension Payment ”), with each such deposit to be made in exchange for a non-interest bearing, unsecured promissory note; WHEREAS , pursuant to Section 6(c) of the Existing Agreement, the Company has obtained the affirmative vote of holders of at least sixty-five percent (65%) of the then outstanding Ordinary Shares and Class B ordinary shares, par value $0.0001 per share, voting together as a single class, approving entry into this Agreement by the Company; and WHEREAS , the Company and the Trustee desire to enter into this Agreement which shall amend and restate the Existing Agreement in its entirety. NOW THEREFORE, IT IS AGREED: 1. Agreements and Covenants of Trustee . The Trustee hereby agrees and covenants to: (a) Hold the Property in trust for the Beneficiaries in accordance with the terms of this Agreement in the Trust Account established by the Trustee located in the United States at J.P. Morgan Chase Bank, N.A. (or at another U.S. chartered commercial bank with consolidated assets of $100 billion or more) and at a brokerage institution selected by the Trustee that is reasonably satisfactory to the Company; (b) Manage, supervise and administer the Trust Account subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein; (c) Promptly upon receipt of written instruction of the Company, (i) invest and reinvest the Property, solely in United States government securities within the meaning of Section 2(a)(16) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, having a maturity of 185 days or less, or in money market funds meeting the conditions of paragraphs (d)(1), (d)(2), (d)(3) and (d)(4) of Rule 2a-7 promulgated under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (or any successor rule), which invest only in direct U.S. government treasury obligations, (ii) hold the Property as uninvested cash or (iii) hold the Property in an non-interest bearing demand deposit account at a U.S. chartered commercial bank with consolidated assets of $100 billion or more selected by the Trustee that is reasonably satisfactory to the Company; it being understood that the Trustee may not invest in any other securities or assets and that the Trust Account will earn no interest while account funds are uninvested awaiting the Company’s instructions hereunder; and while account funds are invested or uninvested, the Trustee may earn bank credits or other consideration during such periods; (d) Collect and receive, when due, all interest or other income arising from the Property, which shall become part of the “ Property ,” as such term is used herein; (e) Promptly notify the Company and Roth of all communications received by the Trustee with respect to any Property requiring action by the Company; (f) Supply any necessary information or documents as may be requested by the Company (or its authorized agents) in connection with the Company’s preparation of tax returns relating to assets held in the Trust Account or in connection with the preparation or completion of the audit of the Company’s financial statements by the Company’s auditors; (g) Participate in any plan or proceeding for protecting or enforcing any right or interest arising from the Property if, as and when instructed by the Company to do so; (h) Render to the Company monthly written statements of the activities of, and amounts in, the Trust Account reflecting all receipts and disbursements of the Trust Account; (i) Commence liquidation of the Trust Account only after and promptly after (x) receipt of, and only in accordance with, the terms of a letter from the Company (“ Termination Letter ”) in a form substantially similar to that attached hereto as either Exhibit A or Exhibit B, jointly signed on behalf of the Company by its Chief Executive Officer, President, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Operating Officer, General Counsel, Secretary or the Chairman of the board of directors of the Company (the “ Board ”) or other authorized officer of the Company and, in the case of Exhibit A, acknowledged and agreed to by Roth, and complete the liquidation of the Trust Account and distribute the Property in the Trust Account, including interest earned thereon and not previously released to the Company to pay its taxes payable or owed (and, in the case of Exhibit B, less an amount of up to $100,000 of interest that may be released to the Company to pay dissolution expenses, it being understood that the Trustee has no obligation to monitor or question the Company’s position that an allocation has been made for taxes payable or owed), only as directed in the Termination Letter and the other documents referred to therein; (y), if a Termination Letter has not been received by the Trustee prior to the earlier of (I) December 11, 2026, as such date may be extended from time to time for one or more Monthly Extension Periods in accordance with the Company’s memorandum and articles of association, as amended and restated from time to time (the “ Memorandum and Articles ”) and Section 1(m) of this Agreement (the “ Deadline ”), and (II) such earlier liquidation date as the Board may approve in accordance with the Memorandum and Articles, or (z) upon the end of a 30-day cure period after the date any additional amount of funds were required to be deposited in the Trust Account as a condition of any extension of such date approved by the Company’s shareholders but were not deposited (such period, the “ Completion Window ”), in which case the Trust Account shall be liquidated in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Termination Letter attached as Exhibit B, and the Property in the Trust Account, including interest not previously released to the Company to pay its taxes, net of taxes payable by the Company and less up to $100,000 of interest that may be released to the Company to pay dissolution expenses, shall be distributed to the Public Shareholders of record as of the applicable date; 2 (j) Upon written request from the Company, which may be given from time to time in a form substantially similar to that attached hereto as Exhibit C (a “ Tax Payment Withdrawal Instruction ”), withdraw from the Trust Account and distribute to the Company the amount of interest earned on the Property requested by the Company to cover any franchise or income tax obligation owed by the Company as a result of assets of the Company or interest or other income earned on the Property, which amount shall be delivered directly to the Company by electronic funds transfer or other method of prompt payment, and the Company shall forward such payment to the relevant taxing authority; provided , however , that to the extent there is not sufficient cash in the Trust Account to pay such tax obligation, the Trustee shall liquidate such assets held in the Trust Account as shall be designated by the Company in writing to make such distribution so long as there is no reduction in the principal amount per share initially deposited in the Trust Account plus any additional amounts, calculated on a per share basis, required to be deposited for an extension of the last date to complete a business combination as a condition of any extension of such date approved by the Company’s shareholders; provided , further , however , that if the tax to be paid is a franchise tax, the written request by the Company to make such distribution shall be accompanied by a copy of the franchise tax bill for the Company and a written statement from the principal financial officer of the Company setting forth the actual amount payable (it being acknowledged and agreed that any such amount in excess of interest income earned on the Property shall not be payable from the Trust Account). The written request of the Company referenced above shall constitute presumptive evidence that the Company is entitled to said funds, and the Trustee shall have no responsibility to look beyond said request; (k) Upon written request from the Company, which may be given from time to time in a form substantially similar to that attached hereto as Exhibit D (a “ Shareholder Redemption Withdrawal Instruction ”), the Trustee shall distribute on behalf of the Company the amount requested by the Company to be used to redeem Ordinary Shares from Public Shareholders properly submitted in connection with a shareholder vote to approve an amendment to the Company’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association (A) to modify the substance or timing of the Company’s obligation to allow redemption in connection with the Company’s initial merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination involving the Company and one or more businesses (a “ Business Combination ”) or to redeem 100% of the Company’s public shares if it does not complete its initial Business Combination by the Deadline or (B) with respect to any other provision relating to shareholders’ rights or pre-initial Business Combination activity. The written request of the Company referenced above shall constitute presumptive evidence that the Company is entitled to distribute said funds, and the Trustee shall have no responsibility to look beyond said request; (l) Not make any withdrawals or distributions from the Trust Account other than pursuant to Section 1(i), (j) or (k) above; and (m) Upon receipt of an extension letter (an “ Extension Letter ”) substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, signed on behalf of the Company by an executive officer and delivered to the Trustee at least five business days prior to the applicable Deadline, and upon receipt in the Trust Account, on or prior to the applicable Deadline, of the applicable Monthly Extension Payment specified in such Extension Letter, follow the instructions set forth in the Extension Letter and deem the Deadline extended by one Monthly Extension Period. 2. Agreements and Covenants of the Company . The Company hereby agrees and covenants to: (a) Give all instructions to the Trustee hereunder in writing, signed by the Chairman of the Board, President, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Operating Officer, General Counsel or Secretary. In addition, except with respect to its duties under Sections 1(i) , 1(j) and 1(k) hereof, the Trustee shall be entitled to rely on, and shall be protected in relying on, any verbal or telephonic advice or instruction which it, in good faith and with reasonable care, believes to be given by any one of the persons authorized above to give written instructions, provided that the Company shall promptly confirm such instructions in writing; 3 (b) Subject to Section 4 hereof, hold the Trustee harmless and indemnify the Trustee from and against any and all reasonable and documented expenses, including reasonable outside counsel fees and disbursements, or losses suffered by the Trustee in connection with any action taken by it hereunder and in connection with any action, suit or other proceeding brought against the Trustee involving any claim, or in connection with any claim or demand, which in any way arises out of or relates to this Agreement, the services of the Trustee hereunder, or the Property or any interest earned on the Property, except for expenses and losses resulting from the Trustee’s gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct. Promptly after the receipt by the Trustee of notice of demand or claim or the commencement of any action, suit or proceeding, pursuant to which the Trustee intends to seek indemnification under this Section 2(b) , it shall notify the Company in writing of such claim (hereinafter referred to as the “ Indemnified Claim ”). The Trustee shall have the right to conduct and manage the defense against such Indemnified Claim; provided that the Trustee shall obtain the consent of the Company with respect to the selection of counsel, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. The Trustee may not agree to settle any Indemnified Claim without the prior written consent of the Company, which such consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. The Company may participate in such action with its own counsel; (c) Pay the Trustee the fees set forth on Schedule A hereto, which fees shall be subject to modification by the parties from time to time. It is expressly understood that the Property shall not be used to pay such fees unless and until the Property is distributed to the Company as permitted by this Agreement. The Company shall not be responsible for any other fees or charges of the Trustee except as set forth in this Section 2(c) and as may be provided in Section 2(b) hereof; (d) In connection with any vote of the Company’s shareholders regarding a Business Combination, provide to the Trustee an affidavit or certificate of the inspector of elections for the shareholder meeting verifying the vote of such shareholders regarding such Business Combination; (e) Provide Roth with a copy of any Termination Letter(s) and/or any other correspondence that is sent to the Trustee with respect to any proposed withdrawal from the Trust Account promptly after it issues the same; (f) Expressly provide in any Instruction Letter (as defined in Exhibit A) delivered in connection with a Termination Letter in the Form of Exhibit A that the Marketing Fee be paid directly to the account or accounts directed by Roth; and (g) Instruct the Trustee to make only those distributions that are permitted under this Agreement, and refrain from instructing the Trustee to make any distributions that are not permitted under this Agreement. 3. Limitations of Liability . The Trustee shall have no responsibility or liability to: (a) Imply obligations, perform duties, inquire or otherwise be subject to the provisions of any agreement or document other than this Agreement and that which is expressly set forth herein; (b) Take any action with respect to the Property, other than as directed in Section 1 hereof, and the Trustee shall have no liability to any party except for liability arising out of the Trustee’s gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct; (c) Institute any proceeding for the collection of any principal and income arising from, or institute, appear in or defend any proceeding of any kind with respect to, any of the Property unless and until it shall have received instructions from the Company given as provided herein to do so and the Company shall have advanced or guaranteed to it funds sufficient to pay any expenses incident thereto; (d) Refund any depreciation in principal of any Property; (e) Assume that the authority of any person designated by the Company to give instructions hereunder shall not be continuing unless provided otherwise in such designation, or unless the Company shall have delivered a written revocation of such authority to the Trustee; 4 (f) Be liable to the other parties hereto or to anyone else for any action taken or omitted by it, or any action suffered by it to be taken or omitted, in good faith and in the Trustee’s best judgment, except for the Trustee’s gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct. The Trustee may rely conclusively and shall be protected in acting upon any order, notice, demand, certificate, opinion or advice of counsel (including counsel chosen by the Trustee with written notification to the Company, which counsel may be the Company’s counsel), statement, instrument, report or other paper or document (not only as to its due execution and the validity and effectiveness of its provisions, but also as to the truth and acceptability of any information therein contained) which the Trustee believes, in good faith and with reasonable care, to be genuine and to be signed or presented by the proper person or persons. The Trustee shall not be bound by any notice or demand, or any waiver, modification, termination or rescission of this Agreement or any of the terms hereof, unless evidenced by a written instrument delivered to the Trustee, signed by the proper party or parties and, if the duties or rights of the Trustee are affected, unless it shall give its prior written consent thereto; (g) Verify the accuracy of the information contained in the Registration Statement; (h) Provide any assurance that any Business Combination entered into by the Company or any other action taken by the Company is as contemplated by the Registration Statement; (i) File information returns with respect to the Trust Account with any local, state or federal taxing authority or provide periodic written statements to the Company documenting the taxes payable by the Company, if any, relating to any interest income earned on the Property; (j) Prepare, execute and file tax reports, income or other tax returns and pay any taxes with respect to any income generated by, and activities relating to, the Trust Account, regardless of whether such tax is payable by the Trust Account or the Company, including, but not limited to, franchise and income tax obligations, except pursuant to Section 1(j) hereof; or (k) Verify calculations, qualify or otherwise approve the Company’s written requests for distributions pursuant to Sections 1(i) , 1(j) or 1(k) hereof. 4. Trust Account Waiver . The Trustee has no right of set-off or any right, title, interest or claim of any kind (“ Claim ”) to, or to any monies in, the Trust Account, and hereby irrevocably waives any Claim to, or to any monies in, the Trust Account that it may have now or in the future. In the event the Trustee has any Claim against the Company under this Agreement, including, without limitation, under Section 2(b) or Section 2(c) hereof, the Trustee shall pursue such Claim solely against the Company and its assets outside the Trust Account and not against the Property or any monies in the Trust Account. 5. Termination . This Agreement shall terminate as follows: (a) If the Trustee gives written notice to the Company that it desires to resign under this Agreement, the Company shall use its reasonable efforts to locate a successor trustee, pending which the Trustee shall continue to act in accordance with this Agreement. At such time that the Company notifies the Trustee that a successor trustee has been appointed and has agreed to become subject to the terms of this Agreement (whether following the Trustee giving notice that it desires to resign under this Agreement or the Company otherwise electing to replace the Trustee under this Agreement), the Trustee shall transfer the management of the Trust Account to the successor trustee, including but not limited to the transfer of copies of the reports and statements relating to the Trust Account, whereupon this Agreement shall terminate; provided , however , that in the event that the Company does not locate a successor trustee within ninety (90) days of receipt of the resignation notice from the Trustee, the Trustee may submit an application to have the Property deposited with any court in the State of New York or with the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York and upon such deposit, the Trustee shall be immune from any liability whatsoever; or (b) At such time that the Trustee has completed the liquidation of the Trust Account and its obligations in accordance with the provisions of Section 1(i) hereof and distributed the Property in accordance with the provisions of the Termination Letter, this Agreement shall terminate except with respect to Section 2(b). 5 6. Miscellaneous . (a) The Company and the Trustee each acknowledge that the Trustee will follow the security procedures set forth below with respect to funds transferred from the Trust Account. The Company and the Trustee will each restrict access to confidential information relating to such security procedures to authorized persons. Each party must notify the other party immediately if it has reason to believe unauthorized persons may have obtained access to such confidential information, or of any change in its authorized personnel. In executing funds transfers, the Trustee shall rely upon all information supplied to it by the Company, including account names, account numbers, and all other identifying information relating to a Beneficiary, Beneficiary’s bank or intermediary bank. Except for any liability arising out of the Trustee’s gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct, the Trustee shall not be liable for any loss, liability or out-of-pocket expense resulting from any error in the information or transmission of the funds. (b) This Agreement shall be governed by and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York. This Agreement may be executed in several original or facsimile counterparts, each one of which shall constitute an original, and together shall constitute but one instrument. (c) This Agreement contains the entire agreement and understanding of the parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof. text: EX-10.2 5 exhibit102-closing8xk.htm EX-10.2 Document Exhibit 10.2 EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT AND INDEMNIFICATION AGREEMENT This Expense Reimbursement and Indemnification Agreement (this “ Agreement ”), dated as of November 20, 2026, is entered into by and between Anthropic, PBC, a Delaware public benefit corporation (the “ Company ”), on the one hand, and Anthropic Founders, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (together with any successor thereto, including any entity resulting from a Reorganization (as defined in the Restated Certificate (as defined below)), the “ Founder LLC ”), on the other hand. The Company and the Founder LLC (the “ Indemnitee Party ”) are each referred to herein individually as a “ Party ” and, collectively, as the “ Parties .” RECITALS WHEREAS, in connection with the initial public offering of the Company’s Class A Common Stock (the “ Public Offering ”), the Company, the Founder LLC and the Anthropic Long-Term Benefit Trust, a Delaware noncharitable purpose trust (the “ Trust ”), have entered into that certain Stockholders’ Agreement, effective as of the IPO Closing Date (as amended or otherwise modified from time to time, the “ Stockholders’ Agreement ”); WHEREAS, Section 3.9 of the Stockholders’ Agreement provides for the advancement, direct payment and reimbursement by the Company of the Expenses (as defined below) of the Founder LLC incurred in connection with Covered Matters (as defined below); WHEREAS, Section 3.10 of the Stockholders’ Agreement requires the Company, in connection with the Public Offering, to execute and deliver an indemnification agreement with the Founder LLC providing for the indemnification of the Founder LLC and its members, among others; WHEREAS, each member of the Founder LLC has entered into an indemnification agreement with the Company in satisfaction of Section 3.10 of the Stockholders’ Agreement; and WHEREAS, this Agreement constitutes the indemnification agreement contemplated by Section 3.10 of the Stockholders’ Agreement with respect to the Founder LLC. AGREEMENT NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing recitals and the covenants and conditions herein set forth, the Parties hereto agree as follows: Section 1. Advancement and Reimbursement of Expenses . (a) As between the Company, on the one hand, and the Founder LLC, on the other hand, the Company shall, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be solely responsible for and shall bear all Expenses (as defined below) incurred in connection with a Covered Matter (as defined below). The Company shall, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, promptly upon, and in any event within thirty (30) days after, the written request of the Founder LLC, advance to the Founder LLC, or pay directly on its behalf, all reasonable and documented out-of-pocket obligations, costs, fees and expenses, including the reasonable fees and expenses of counsel (collectively, the “ Expenses ”) incurred in connection with (i) the administration and maintenance of the Founder LLC, including tax returns and filings (including, but not limited to, FBAR filings and other regulatory filings) and any taxes, fees or similar charges incurred by the Founder LLC; (ii) the ownership, voting or disposition of the Shares (as defined in the Stockholders’ Agreement), including the appraisal thereof; (iii) the exercise or performance of, or the failure to exercise or perform, any right, power, duty or obligation under the Stockholders’ Agreement, the Company’s Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation, duly adopted and filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware in connection with the Public Offering (as it may be amended or otherwise modified from time to time, the “ Restated Certificate ”), the Company’s bylaws (as amended from time to time, the “ Bylaws ”), the Limited Liability Company Agreement of the Founder LLC, dated as of November 20, 2026 (as amended or restated from time to time, the “ Founder LLC Agreement ”), the Amended and Restated Trust Agreement of the Trust, in effect as of the time of the Public Offering (as it may be amended or otherwise modified from time to time, the “ Trust Agreement ”) or the Amended and Restated Resource and Information Agreement, dated as of November 20, 2026, by and between the Company and the Trust (as amended or restated from time to time, the “ Resource Agreement ”); (iv) the dissolution, winding up or termination of, or any post-termination liability in respect of, the Founder LLC; (v) the formation, structuring, negotiation, documentation, execution, delivery or amendment of the Stockholders’ Agreement, the Restated Certificate, the Bylaws, the Founder LLC Agreement, the Trust Agreement, the Resource Agreement, the Class E Common Stock Documentation (as defined in the Stockholders’ Agreement) or this Agreement, or any Reorganization; (vi) the Public Offering (including any actual or alleged statement or omission in the registration statement, any prospectus (including the founders’ letter included therein) or any other offering materials or communications relating thereto, regardless of the capacity in which any Founder LLC Indemnitee acted or is alleged to have acted) or (vii) any Proceeding (as defined below) to establish, enforce or interpret any right to indemnification or advancement of expenses of any Founder LLC Indemnitee under this Agreement, the Stockholders’ Agreement, the Restated Certificate, the Bylaws, any indemnification agreement between the Company and any Founder LLC Indemnitee or any other agreement with the Company (each of clauses (i) through (vii), a “ Covered Matter ”). Without limiting the foregoing, Expenses shall include all reasonable and documented (A) fees and expenses of experts, witnesses, accountants, consultants and appraisers, (B) electronic discovery and document production costs, (C) travel and meeting costs of the members of the Founder LLC incurred in connection with any Covered Matter and (D) costs and expenses incurred in investigating, defending, being a witness or deponent in or otherwise participating in any Proceeding arising out of or relating to any Covered Matter, which shall in all cases be advanced, paid or reimbursed under this Section 1 . “ Proceeding ” means any threatened, pending or completed action, suit, arbitration, mediation, alternate dispute resolution mechanism, claim or threatened claim, cause of action, investigation, inquiry, hearing or other proceeding. To the extent any such Expense has already been paid by the Founder LLC, the Company shall instead reimburse the Founder LLC within thirty (30) days following a written request therefor. (b) The Founder LLC shall not be required to incur any liability, or to advance any funds, in respect of any Covered Matter other than from amounts provided by the Company. 2 (c) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, advancement or reimbursement of the Expenses will not be required in respect of amounts (i) determined by a final non-appealable judgment or order of a court of competent jurisdiction (A) not to have been reasonably related to a Covered Matter or (B) to have resulted from the actual fraud or willful misconduct of the Founder LLC or the applicable Founder LLC Indemnitee; provided that the actual fraud or willful misconduct of any Founder LLC Indemnitee shall not be imputed to any other Founder LLC Indemnitee (other than to the Founder LLC, with respect to any authorized act or omission by or on behalf of the Founder LLC); (ii) incurred in connection with any Proceeding (or any part thereof) initiated by the Founder LLC or any other Founder LLC Indemnitee against the Company, any of its subsidiaries or any of their respective directors or officers (in their capacities as such), unless (A) the Company’s board of directors authorized the Proceeding (or the relevant part thereof) prior to its initiation, (B) the Company provides the indemnification, in its sole discretion, or (C) the Proceeding (or the relevant part thereof) constitutes a Covered Matter pursuant to clause (vii) of Section 1(a); or (iii) constituting any judgment, award, fine, penalty, amount paid in settlement or award of fees or costs, in each case payable to the Company or any of its subsidiaries by the Founder LLC or any other Founder LLC Indemnitee. Section 2. Indemnification of Founder LLC Indemnitees; Advancement of Expenses . (a) The Company agrees to indemnify, defend, exonerate and hold harmless, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, the Founder LLC and each of the Founder LLC’s former, current and future affiliates, officers, directors, managers, trustees, partners, members, stockholders, employees, agents and representatives, each Estate Successor (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement), in the case of any member of the Founder LLC, each Family Member (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) thereof, each Company Designated Official (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement), and each of the Covered Persons (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) (collectively, the “ Founder LLC Indemnitees ”) from and against any and all threatened, pending or completed Proceedings, in each case whether a Founder LLC Indemnitee is involved as a party, witness, deponent or otherwise, and any and all liabilities, losses, damages, judgments, fines and penalties (in each case, to the extent indemnification thereof is permitted by applicable law), amounts paid in settlement, reasonable and documented costs and expenses (including, without limitation, reasonable and documented attorneys’, accountants’, experts’ and consultants’ fees, expenses and disbursements) incurred by the Founder LLC Indemnitees or any of them before, on or after the date of this Agreement, arising out of or in any way relating to any Covered Matter (the “ Indemnified Liabilities ”); provided that the foregoing indemnification rights will not be available to a Founder LLC Indemnitee to the extent that a court of competent jurisdiction determines by final non-appealable judgment or order that such Indemnified Liabilities arose on account of such Founder LLC Indemnitee’s actual fraud or willful misconduct (which shall not be imputed to any other Founder LLC Indemnitee (other than to the Founder LLC, with respect to any authorized act or omission by or on behalf of the Founder LLC)); and provided , further , that if and to the extent that the foregoing indemnification rights may be unavailable or unenforceable for any reason (other than the actual fraud or willful misconduct of the applicable Founder LLC Indemnitee), the Company hereby agrees to make the maximum contribution to the payment and satisfaction of each of the 3 Indemnified Liabilities which is permissible under applicable law. The Company shall be obligated to pay in cash promptly, and in any event within thirty (30) days after written request therefor, all expenses and other costs incident to any actual or threatened Proceeding, including those incurred in defending any civil or criminal action arising out of or relating to any event or circumstance to which this Section 2 shall apply. Any payment under this Agreement to any Founder LLC Indemnitee shall be made upon receipt of an undertaking by or on behalf of such Founder LLC Indemnitee to repay such amount if it shall ultimately be determined by a final non-appealable judgment or order of a court of competent jurisdiction that such Founder LLC Indemnitee was not entitled to such payment under this Agreement, which undertaking shall be unsecured and interest-free and shall be accepted without reference to such Founder LLC Indemnitee’s financial ability to make repayment. (b) The Company will reimburse each Founder LLC Indemnitee, within thirty (30) days after written request therefor, for all reasonable and documented costs and expenses (including reasonable and documented attorneys’ and experts’ fees and expenses and any other litigation-related expenses) as they are incurred in connection with investigating, preparing, pursuing, defending or assisting in the defense of any Proceeding for which the Founder LLC Indemnitee would be entitled to indemnification under the terms of Section 2(a) , or any claim, action or proceeding arising therefrom, whether such Founder LLC Indemnitee is involved as a party, witness, deponent or otherwise. The Company agrees that it will not, without the prior written consent of the Founder LLC Indemnitee, settle, compromise or consent to the entry of any judgment in any pending or threatened Proceeding relating to the matters contemplated hereby (if any Founder LLC Indemnitee is a party thereto or has been threatened to be made a party thereto) unless such settlement, compromise or consent includes an unconditional release of the Founder LLC Indemnitee from all liability, without future obligation or prohibition on the part of the Founder LLC Indemnitee, arising or that may arise out of such Proceeding, and does not contain an admission of guilt or liability on the part of the Founder LLC Indemnitee. (c) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Company shall not be liable to any Founder LLC Indemnitee in respect of any Indemnified Liabilities (or any related costs and expenses) to the extent the same are determined, by a final non-appealable judgment or order of a court of competent jurisdiction, to have resulted from the actual fraud or willful misconduct of such Founder LLC Indemnitee, which shall not be imputed to any other Founder LLC Indemnitee (other than to the Founder LLC, with respect to any authorized act or omission by or on behalf of the Founder LLC). An adverse judgment or plea of nolo contendere shall not, of itself, create a presumption that any Founder LLC Indemnitee committed actual fraud or willful misconduct. Without limiting the foregoing, and notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Company shall not be obligated to indemnify, advance or reimburse any amounts to, or make any contribution on behalf of, any Founder LLC Indemnitee in respect of any amounts of the type described in Section 1(c)(ii) or Section 1(c)(iii) (other than costs and expenses incurred in any Proceeding to establish or enforce any right to indemnification or advancement under this Section 2 ). (d) For purposes of this Agreement, (i) no act or omission shall constitute “willful misconduct” unless done or omitted not in good faith and with actual knowledge that such act or 4 omission was wrongful; (ii) any act or omission based upon authority given pursuant to a resolution duly adopted by the Company’s board of directors (or a committee thereof), or upon the advice of counsel, shall be conclusively presumed to have been done or omitted in good faith; (iii) “actual fraud” means actual and intentional common law fraud under Delaware law, excluding for the avoidance of doubt any claims based on negligence, recklessness or constructive knowledge; and (iv) actual fraud or willful misconduct shall be established only by clear and convincing evidence. (e) In any claim, action or proceeding to establish, enforce or interpret any right to indemnification or advancement of expenses hereunder, each Founder LLC Indemnitee shall be presumed to be entitled thereto, and the Company shall bear the burden of proving, by clear and convincing evidence, that such Founder LLC Indemnitee is not so entitled. (f) The rights of any Founder LLC Indemnitee to indemnification hereunder will be in addition to any other rights any such person may have under the Stockholders’ Agreement (including Section 3.9 thereof) or any other agreement or instrument to which such Founder LLC Indemnitee is or becomes a party or is or otherwise becomes a beneficiary or under applicable law or regulation. The Company hereby acknowledges that each Founder LLC Indemnitee may have certain rights to indemnification, advancement of expenses and/or insurance provided by one or more persons or entities with whom or which such Founder LLC Indemnitee may be associated (including, without limitation, any other Founder LLC Indemnitee). The Company hereby acknowledges and agrees that (i) the Company shall be the indemnitor of first resort with respect to any Indemnified Liability, (ii) the Company shall be primarily liable for all Indemnified Liabilities and any indemnification afforded to any Founder LLC Indemnitee in respect of any Indemnified Liabilities, whether created by law, organizational or constituent documents, contract (including this Agreement) or otherwise, (iii) any obligation of any such other person or entity to indemnify such Founder LLC Indemnitee and/or advance expenses to such Founder LLC Indemnitee in respect of any Proceeding shall be secondary to the obligations of the Company hereunder, (iv) the Company shall be required to indemnify each Founder LLC Indemnitee and advance expenses to each Founder LLC Indemnitee hereunder to the fullest extent provided herein without regard to any rights such Founder LLC Indemnitee may have against any such other person or entity or insurer of any such person or entity and (v) the Company (on behalf of itself and its insurers) irrevocably waives, relinquishes and releases any such other person or entity from any claim of contribution, subrogation or any other recovery of any kind in respect of amounts paid by the Company hereunder. In the event any such other person or entity or its insurers advance or extinguish any liability or loss which is the subject of any Indemnified Liability owed by the Company, the payor shall have a right of subrogation against the Company or its insurer or insurers for all amounts so paid which would otherwise be payable by the Company or its insurer or insurers under this Agreement. In no event will payment of an Indemnified Liability under this Agreement by any such other person or entity or its insurers affect the obligations of the Company hereunder or shift primary liability for any Indemnified Liability to any other person or entity. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company shall not be liable under this Agreement to make any payment to or on behalf of any Founder LLC Indemnitee to the extent such Founder LLC Indemnitee has actually received 5 payment of such amount under any other indemnification agreement with the Company, the Restated Certificate, the Bylaws or any insurance policy maintained by the Company. (g) The indemnity rights provided to the Founder LLC Indemnitees under this Agreement are cumulative with, and do not supersede, any other indemnification rights such Founder LLC Indemnitees would have at common law or under any other agreement or arrangement and shall remain in full force and effect following any termination of this Agreement. (h) The Company shall at all times maintain, or cause to be available, funds sufficient to satisfy its obligations under this Agreement as and when due, and shall not take any action that would reasonably be expected to impair its ability to timely satisfy such obligations. (i) Each Founder LLC Indemnitee shall have the right to control the defense of any Proceeding against such Founder LLC Indemnitee with counsel of its choosing, and the reasonable fees and expenses of such counsel shall constitute Indemnified Liabilities. If the Company assumes the defense of any such Proceeding with the consent of the applicable Founder LLC Indemnitee, such Founder LLC Indemnitee may nonetheless retain separate counsel at the Company’s expense if (i) such Founder LLC Indemnitee reasonably concludes that a conflict of interest may exist between the Company and such Founder LLC Indemnitee in the conduct of such defense or (ii) the Company fails to employ counsel reasonably satisfactory to such Founder LLC Indemnitee. The Company shall promptly notify the Indemnitee Party in writing of any threatened or pending Proceeding of which the Company becomes aware that may give rise to a Covered Matter or an Indemnified Liability, and shall promptly provide copies of all material correspondence and pleadings relating thereto. (j) Except as expressly provided in Sections 1(c) and 2(c) , the obligations of the Company under this Agreement are absolute and unconditional and shall not be subject to any set-off, counterclaim, recoupment, defense or other right that the Company or any of its subsidiaries may have against the Founder LLC or any Founder LLC Indemnitee. To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, the Company irrevocably waives, and agrees not to assert, any claim or defense that this Agreement or any provision hereof is invalid, unenforceable, contrary to public policy or not binding on the Company. The obligations of the Company hereunder shall not be released, discharged, impaired or otherwise affected by any bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization or similar proceeding of the Company, any change of control of the Company or any change in the composition of the Company’s board of directors. Section 3. Taxes . Any and all payments required to be made to the Founder LLC or any other Founder LLC Indemnitee (each, a “ Recipient ”) hereunder shall be made free and clear of, and without deduction for, any federal, state, local, foreign or other taxes, duties and assessments in the nature of a tax imposed by a governmental entity or tax authority (“ Taxes ”); provided , however , that, if the Company shall be required by applicable law to deduct any Taxes from any payment hereunder, (i) such payment shall be increased as necessary so that, after making all required deductions (including deductions applicable to additional amounts payable under this Section 3 ), the Recipient receives payments equal to the amount it would have received had no such deductions been made, (ii) the Company shall make such deductions and 6 (iii) the Company shall pay the full amount deducted to the relevant governmental authority in accordance with applicable law. Each Recipient shall provide to the Company an IRS Form W-9 or applicable IRS Form W-8 prior to or simultaneously with any payments to be made hereunder and at such other times reasonably requested by the Company. Section 4. Term and Termination . (a) Term . This Agreement will be effective from the date hereof and will remain in effect until terminated pursuant to Section 4(b) . The date on which this Agreement is so terminated is referred to herein as the “ Termination Date .” (b) Termination of Agreement . This Agreement may be terminated at any time by the mutual written consent of the Indemnitee Party and the Company. For the avoidance of doubt, the termination of the Stockholders’ Agreement shall not, in and of itself, terminate this Agreement. Subject to Section 4(c) , this Agreement shall automatically terminate upon the later to occur of (i) the Class F Sunset Time (as defined in the Restated Certificate) and (ii) the completion of the winding up of the Founder LLC and the filing of its certificate of cancellation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. (c) Effect of Termination . Upon the Termination Date, all rights and obligations of each of the Company and the Founder LLC Indemnitees shall immediately cease and terminate, and no Party shall have any further obligation to the other Party with respect to this Agreement, except that (i) the rights and obligations in Section 1 , Section 2 , Section 3 , Section 9 and Section 12 of this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement, and shall continue, with respect to any Covered Matter or any Proceeding arising out of any act, omission or circumstance occurring on or prior to the Termination Date (including any Covered Matter relating to the dissolution, winding up or termination of, or any post-termination liability in respect of, the Founder LLC); and (ii) the termination of this Agreement will not relieve any Party from liability for any breach of this Agreement on or prior to the Termination Date. Section 5. Amendments and Waivers . No amendment or waiver of any provision of this Agreement, or consent to any departure by either Party from any such provision, shall be effective unless the same shall be in writing and signed by each Party to this Agreement, and, in any case, such amendment, waiver or consent shall be effective only in the specific instance and for the specific purpose for which given; provided that no amendment, waiver or consent that would adversely affect the rights of any Founder LLC Indemnitee hereunder shall be effective as to such Founder LLC Indemnitee without such Founder LLC Indemnitee’s prior written consent. The waiver by any Party of any breach of this Agreement shall not operate as or be construed to be a waiver by such Party of any subsequent breach. Section 6. Assignment; Third-Party Beneficiaries . This Agreement and the rights of the Parties hereunder may not be assigned without the prior written consent of each of the Parties hereto. Subject to the foregoing, the provisions of this Agreement will be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties hereto and their respective successors and assigns. The Company shall require any successor (whether direct or indirect, by purchase, merger, consolidation, conversion, division, operation of law or otherwise) to all or substantially all of 7 the business or assets of the Company to expressly assume and agree to perform this Agreement in the same manner and to the same extent that the Company would be required to perform if no such succession had taken place, and references herein to the Company shall include any such successor. Subject to the next sentence, no person or party other than the Parties hereto and their respective successors or permitted assigns is intended to be a beneficiary of this Agreement. The Parties acknowledge and agree that each of the Founder LLC Indemnitees shall be third-party beneficiaries of this Agreement, in each case entitled to enforce this Agreement as though each such Founder LLC Indemnitee were a party to this Agreement. Section 7. Notices . Any and all notices hereunder shall be deemed duly given when delivered by registered or certified mail (postage prepaid), email, overnight courier or hand delivery to the Parties at the following addresses (or such different addresses as are specified by a Party for itself by notice to the other Party in accordance with this Section 7 ): If to the Company: Anthropic, PBC 548 Market Street, PMB 90375 San Francisco, CA 94104 Attention: Legal Department Email: notices@anthropic.com with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to: Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, P.C. [***] Attention: [***] Email: [***] If to the Founder LLC: Anthropic Founders, LLC c/o Anthropic, PBC 548 Market Street, PMB 90375 San Francisco, CA 94104 Attention: Legal Department Email: notices@anthropic.com with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to: Cravath, Swaine & Moore LLP [***] Attention: [***] Email: [***] Section 8. Entire Agreement . This Agreement, together with the Stockholders’ Agreement, the Restated Certificate, the Bylaws, the Founder LLC Agreement, the Trust 8 Agreement, the Resource Agreement and any other indemnification agreement entered into between the Parties pursuant to Section 3.10 of the Stockholders’ Agreement, constitutes the full and entire understanding and agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, and any other written or oral agreements relating to the subject matter hereof existing between or among any of the Parties are expressly canceled; provided that nothing in this Agreement shall cancel, supersede or limit (i) any agreement or arrangement providing for the payment or reimbursement by the Company of fees and expenses incurred by the Founder LLC or its members in connection with the structuring and negotiation of the governance arrangements of the Company prior to the Public Offering or (ii) any right to indemnification, advancement of expenses or insurance of any Founder LLC Indemnitee under applicable law, the Restated Certificate, the Bylaws or any indemnification agreement between the Company and any Founder LLC Indemnitee. Section 9. Governing Law; Consent to Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial . (a) Governing Law . This Agreement shall be interpreted, construed and governed by and in accordance with the internal law of the State of Delaware, without regard to any conflict of law principles thereof that otherwise would result in the application of the laws of another jurisdiction. (b) Consent to Jurisdiction . In any claim, action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement, each of the Parties hereto (A) irrevocably and unconditionally consents and submits to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware; (B) agrees that it will not attempt to deny or defeat such jurisdiction by motion or other request for leave from such court; and (C) agrees that it will not bring any such action in any court other than the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, or, if (and only if) such court finds it lacks subject matter jurisdiction, another State court in Delaware or the Federal court of the United States of America sitting in Delaware, and appellate courts thereof. Service of process, summons, notice or document to any Party’s address and in the manner set forth in Section 7 shall be effective service of process for any such action. (c) Waiver of Jury Trial . EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN RESPECT OF ANY LITIGATION DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT. Section 10. Counterparts; Electronic Signatures . This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts, and by different Parties on separate counterparts. Each set of counterparts showing execution by all Parties shall be deemed an original, and shall constitute one and the same instrument. The words “execution,” “signed,” “signature,” and words of like import in this Agreement shall include images of manually executed signatures transmitted by electronic format (including, without limitation, “pdf,” “tif” or “jpg”) and other electronic signatures (including, without limitation, DocuSign and AdobeSign). The use of electronic signatures and electronic records (including, without limitation, any contract or other record created, generated, sent, communicated, received, or stored by electronic means) shall be of the same legal effect, validity and enforceability as a manually executed signature or use of a paper- 9 based record-keeping system to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, including the Federal Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act and any other applicable law, including, without limitation, any state law based on the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act or the Uniform Commercial Code. Section 11. Severability . If any provision or provisions of this Agreement shall be held to be invalid or unenforceable, the validity, legality and enforceability of the remaining provisions hereof shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby. Section 12. Specific Performance . The Company acknowledges and agrees that any failure by the Company to timely advance, pay or reimburse any amount required to be advanced, paid or reimbursed hereunder, or otherwise to perform its obligations hereunder in accordance with their specific terms, would cause irreparable harm to the Founder LLC Indemnitees for which monetary damages, even if available, would not be an adequate remedy. Accordingly, each Founder LLC Indemnitee shall be entitled to an injunction or injunctions, specific performance and other equitable relief to prevent breaches of this Agreement and to enforce specifically its terms, without proof of actual damages and without any requirement to post a bond or other security, in addition to any other remedy to which it is entitled at law or in equity. The Company agrees not to assert that a remedy of specific enforcement is unenforceable, invalid, contrary to applicable law or inequitable for any reason, and agrees not to oppose any request by a Founder LLC Indemnitee for expedited or summary proceedings to enforce any right to advancement, payment, reimbursement or indemnification hereunder.
